claim: TRPM7 is a ubiquitously expressed membrane protein consisting of ion channel and protein kinase domains.
source: The transient receptor potential melastatin-subfamily member 7 (TRPM7) is a ubiquitously expressed membrane protein consisting of ion channel and protein kinase domains.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known characteristic of TRPM7.

claim: TRPM7 plays a fundamental role in the cellular uptake of divalent cations such as Zn2+, Mg2+, and Ca2+.
source: TRPM7 plays a fundamental role in the cellular uptake of divalent cations such as Zn2+, Mg2+, and Ca2+, and thus shapes cellular excitability, plasticity, and metabolic activity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established function of TRPM7.

claim: TRPM7 shapes cellular excitability, plasticity, and metabolic activity.
source: TRPM7 plays a fundamental role in the cellular uptake of divalent cations such as Zn2+, Mg2+, and Ca2+, and thus shapes cellular excitability, plasticity, and metabolic activity.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of TRPM7's role in divalent cation uptake.

claim: Native TRPM7 channels are high-molecular-weight multi-protein complexes that contain CNNM1-4 and ARL15.
source: We found that native TRPM7 channels are high-molecular-weight multi-protein complexes that contain the putative metal transporter proteins CNNM1-4 and a small G-protein ADP-ribosylation factor-like protein 15 (ARL15).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on multi-epitope affinity purification and mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: Complex formation of TRPM7 with CNNM and ARL15 effectively and specifically impacts TRPM7 activity.
source: Heterologous reconstitution experiments confirmed the formation of TRPM7/CNNM/ARL15 ternary complexes and indicated that complex formation effectively and specifically impacts TRPM7 activity.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from heterologous reconstitution experiments.

claim: TRPM6 is the only other known channel-kinase that shows a similar design to TRPM7.
source: Among all other known channels and kinases, only its homologue TPRM6 shows a similar design (Ryazanov et al., 1997; Chubanov and Gudermann, 2014).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: TRPM7 is involved in various cellular processes such as homeostatic balance, cell motility, proliferation, differentiation, and regulation of immune responses.
source: TRPM7 is involved in various cellular processes such as homeostatic balance, cell motility, proliferation, differentiation, and regulation of immune responses (Chubanov et al., 2018; Fleig and Chubanov, 2014; Ryazanov et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: Genetic deletion of Trpm7 in mice is embryonically lethal.
source: Genetic deletion of Trpm7 in mice is embryonically lethal, and tissue-specific null mutants have shown defects in cardiac and renal morphogenesis, organismal Zn2+, Mg2+, and Ca2+ homeostasis, thrombopoiesis, and mast cell degranulation (Mittermeier et al., 2019; Chubanov et al., 2004; Jin et al., 2008; Sah et al., 2013b; Sah et al., 2013a; Jin et al., 2012; Stritt et al., 2016; Abiria et al., 2017; Schmitz et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: Tissue-specific TRPM7 null mutants have shown defects in cardiac and renal morphogenesis, organismal Zn2+, Mg2+, and Ca2+ homeostasis, thrombopoiesis, and mast cell degranulation.
source: Genetic deletion of Trpm7 in mice is embryonically lethal, and tissue-specific null mutants have shown defects in cardiac and renal morphogenesis, organismal Zn2+, Mg2+, and Ca2+ homeostasis, thrombopoiesis, and mast cell degranulation (Mittermeier et al., 2019; Chubanov et al., 2004; Jin et al., 2008; Sah et al., 2013b; Sah et al., 2013a; Jin et al., 2012; Stritt et al., 2016; Abiria et al., 2017; Schmitz et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: TRPM7 has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for numerous pathophysiological conditions.
source: Besides, TRPM7 has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for numerous pathophysiological conditions (Chubanov et al., 2018; Fleig and Chubanov, 2014; Ryazanov et al., 1997; Hofmann et al., 2014; Aarts et al., 2003; Hermosura et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: The channel-coding segment of TRPM7 comprises six transmembrane helices with a pore-loop sequence between S5 and S6.
source: The channel-coding segment of TRPM7 comprises six transmembrane helices with a pore-loop sequence between S5 and S6 (Figure 1A, Duan et al., 2018; Mederos y Schnitzler et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1A and supporting citations.

claim: Four TRPM7 subunits assemble to form constitutively active channels highly selective for divalent cations such as Zn2+, Ca2+, and Mg2+.
source: Four subunits assemble to form constitutively active channels highly selective for divalent cations such as Zn2+, Ca2+, and Mg2+ (Nadler et al., 2001; Runnels et al., 2001; Monteilh-Zoller et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: Free Mg2+, the Mg·ATP complex, and phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) were described as physiological regulators of the channel activity of TRPM7.
source: Free Mg2+, the Mg·ATP complex, and phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) were described as physiological regulators of the channel activity of TRPM7 (Nadler et al., 2001; Runnels et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: Mg2+ or Mg·ATP act as negative regulators of TRPM7 channel activity.
source: While Mg2+ or Mg·ATP act as negative regulators, PIP2 appears to be a crucial co-factor of the active channel (Nadler et al., 2001; Runnels et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: PIP2 appears to be a crucial co-factor of the active TRPM7 channel.
source: While Mg2+ or Mg·ATP act as negative regulators, PIP2 appears to be a crucial co-factor of the active channel (Nadler et al., 2001; Runnels et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: The effects of Mg2+, Mg·ATP, or PIP2 on TRPM7 activity are poorly understood.
source: Mechanistically, however, the effects of Mg2+, Mg·ATP, or PIP2 on TRPM7 activity are poorly understood, and most likely, there are additional regulators of TRPM7 function with hitherto unknown molecular identity.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: There are likely additional regulators of TRPM7 function with hitherto unknown molecular identity.
source: Mechanistically, however, the effects of Mg2+, Mg·ATP, or PIP2 on TRPM7 activity are poorly understood, and most likely, there are additional regulators of TRPM7 function with hitherto unknown molecular identity.
evidence: This is stated as speculation based on current knowledge gaps.

claim: Native TRPM7 channels in HEK293 cells have an apparent molecular mass of at least 1.2 MDa.
source: Unexpectedly, analysis by native gel electrophoresis (BN-PAGE) of TRPM7 channels either endogenous to HEK293 cells or exogenously expressed in these cells via transient transfection, elicited a molecular mass of at least 1.2 MDa considerably exceeding the molecular mass of ~850 kDa calculated for TRPM7 tetramers (Figure 1B, upper panel).
evidence: This is a finding from BN-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The apparent molecular mass of native TRPM7 channels considerably exceeds the molecular mass of ~850 kDa calculated for TRPM7 tetramers.
source: Unexpectedly, analysis by native gel electrophoresis (BN-PAGE) of TRPM7 channels either endogenous to HEK293 cells or exogenously expressed in these cells via transient transfection, elicited a molecular mass of at least 1.2 MDa considerably exceeding the molecular mass of ~850 kDa calculated for TRPM7 tetramers (Figure 1B, upper panel).
evidence: This is a finding from BN-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: TRPM7 in mouse brain has an apparent molecular mass between 1.2 and 2.6 MDa.
source: As illustrated in Figure 1B, lower panel, csBN-MS analysis of mouse brain membranes detected the TRPM7 protein with an apparent molecular mass between 1.2 and 2.6 MDa, comparable to the results obtained from HEK293 cells (Figure 1B, upper panel).
evidence: This is a finding from csBN-MS analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: TRPM7 levels in the brain are rather low compared to other members of the TRP family of proteins.
source: Moreover, the determination of the total protein amount by signal integration over all slices showed that TRPM7 levels in the brain are rather low compared to other members of the TRP family of proteins.
evidence: This is a finding from quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: The abundance of TRPM7 is about one to three orders of magnitude below that obtained for TRPC4, TRPM3, or TRPV2.
source: Thus, the abundance of TRPM7 is about one to three orders of magnitude below that obtained for TRPC4, TRPM3, or TRPV2 (Figure 1B, lower right).
evidence: This is a finding from quantitative mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Native TRPM7 complexes exceed the predicted molecular size of bare tetrameric assemblies in different cellular environments.
source: Together, these results indicated that native TRPM7 complexes exceed the predicted molecular size of bare tetrameric assemblies in different cellular environments suggesting that the rather simplistic view on the molecular make-up of native TRPM7 channel complexes has to be revised.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the BN-PAGE and csBN-MS data.

claim: ARL15 and CNNM1-4 were identified as high-confidence interaction partners of TRPM7.
source: Together, these specificity and consistency criteria identified five proteins as high-confidence interaction partners of TRPM7: ARL15 and the cyclin M family proteins CNNM1-4, putative Mg2+ transporters (Figure 1C, Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from ME-AP experiments shown in Figure 1C and Table 1.

claim: CNNM1-4 are putative Mg2+ transporters.
source: Together, these specificity and consistency criteria identified five proteins as high-confidence interaction partners of TRPM7: ARL15 and the cyclin M family proteins CNNM1-4, putative Mg2+ transporters (Figure 1C, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of CNNM proteins.

claim: ARL15 and CNNMs were not detected in any of the negative controls.
source: Neither of these proteins was detected in any of the negative controls.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the specificity analysis of the ME-AP experiments.

claim: The interaction between TRPM7, ARL15, and CNNMs was weakened by the more stringent detergent CL-91.
source: Comparison of the degree of association under the two solubilisation conditions revealed that the interaction between TRPM7, ARL15, and CNNMs was weakened by the more stringent detergent CL-91 (Figure 1C, Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing ME-AP results under different solubilization conditions.

claim: Flag-tagged ARL15 and CNNM proteins could be specifically and robustly co-purified with HA-tagged TRPM7 when all three proteins were present.
source: Flag-tagged ARL15 and CNNM proteins could be specifically and robustly co-purified with HA-tagged TRPM7 in anti-HA APs when all three proteins were present, whereas the association was markedly less efficient when ARL15-Flag or CNNM-Flag were co-expressed with TRPM7-HA alone (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from co-expression experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: The association of ARL15 or CNNM with TRPM7 was markedly less efficient when ARL15-Flag or CNNM-Flag were co-expressed with TRPM7-HA alone.
source: Flag-tagged ARL15 and CNNM proteins could be specifically and robustly co-purified with HA-tagged TRPM7 in anti-HA APs when all three proteins were present, whereas the association was markedly less efficient when ARL15-Flag or CNNM-Flag were co-expressed with TRPM7-HA alone (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from co-expression experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: TRPM7, ARL15, and CNNM proteins form ternary complexes.
source: These results corroborated the ME-AP results from the rodent brain and strongly suggested the formation of ternary complexes containing TRPM7, ARL15, and CNNM proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the co-expression experiments.

claim: Co-expression of TRPM7 and CNNM3 did not change the shape of the I-V relationship or current amplitudes.
source: Co-expression of TRPM7 and CNNM3, the most efficiently co-purified CNNM protein (Figure 1C), neither changed the shape of the I-V relationship nor current amplitudes.
evidence: This is a finding from TEVC measurements in Xenopus oocytes.

claim: ARL15 effectively suppressed constitutive TRPM7 currents in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: In contrast, ARL15 effectively suppressed constitutive TRPM7 currents in a concentration-dependent manner, as deduced from experiments with increasing amounts of ARL15 (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from TEVC measurements shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Oocytes co-expressing TRPM7, CNNM3, and ARL15 did not exhibit TRPM7 currents.
source: Oocytes co-expressing all three proteins TRPM7, CNNM3, and ARL15 did not exhibit TRPM7 currents, similar to the co-expression of TRPM7 and ARL15 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from TEVC measurements shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The suppressive effect of ARL15 on TRPM7 was specific for TRPM7.
source: The suppressive effect was specific for TRPM7, as co-expressed ARL15 did not inhibit another TRP channel, TRPV1, in an analogous experiment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from control experiments with TRPV1 shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Co-expression of TRPM7 with ARL8A did not affect TRPM7 currents.
source: Consistently, co-expression of TRPM7 with another ARL family member, ARL8A (Gillingham and Munro, 2007), did not affect TRPM7 currents (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from control experiments with ARL8A shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Co-expression of ARL15 did not change the expression level of TRPM7 protein.
source: Western blot analysis of oocytes injected with Trpm7 or Trpm7 and Arl15 cRNAs did not reveal any change in the expression level of TRPM7 protein (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: TRPM7 was similarly detectable at the cell surface of oocytes co-expressing TRPM7 and ARL15.
source: Notably, the TRPM7 signal was similarly detectable at the cell surface of oocytes co-expressing TRPM7 and ARL15 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 3E.

claim: ARL15 acted similarly on inward and outward TRPM7 currents.
source: This analysis revealed that ARL15 acted similarly on inward and outward TRPM7 currents, suggesting that ARL15 elicited a general block of the TRPM7 channel.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of inward and outward currents.

claim: ARL15 elicited a general block of the TRPM7 channel.
source: This analysis revealed that ARL15 acted similarly on inward and outward TRPM7 currents, suggesting that ARL15 elicited a general block of the TRPM7 channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of inward and outward currents.

claim: The K1646R mutation did not change the sensitivity of TRPM7 for the inhibitory effect of ARL15.
source: To this end, we examined oocytes expressing a kinase-dead TRPM7 mutant (K1646R, Nadler et al., 2001; Runnels et al., 2002) and observed that the K1646R mutation did not change the sensitivity of TRPM7 for the inhibitory effect of ARL15 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments with the K1646R mutant shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Transient expression of ARL15 caused a significant reduction of endogenous TRPM7 currents in HEK293 cells.
source: Transient expression of ARL15 however caused a significant reduction of these TRPM7 currents (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from patch-clamp experiments in HEK293 cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The inhibitory effect of ARL15 on TRPM7 currents is specific and concentration-dependent.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that the inhibitory effect of ARL15 on TRPM7 currents is specific and concentration-dependent.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments.

claim: Co-expression of ARL15 suppressed TRPM7 Mg2+ currents.
source: TRPM7 expressing oocytes displayed characteristic TRPM7 currents with a very small inward Mg2+ component, which was suppressed by co-expression of ARL15 (Figure 4A and B) in accord with previous experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This is a finding from TEVC measurements with Mg2+ shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Co-expression of CNNM3 did not change the properties of the TRPM7 channel in the presence of Mg2+.
source: In contrast, co-expression of CNNM3 did not change the properties of the TRPM7 channel (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from TEVC measurements with Mg2+ shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Co-expression of TRPM7 and CNNM3 showed similar results to TRPM7 alone in response to 10 mM Mg2+ perfusion.
source: Corresponding experiments with cells co-expressing TRPM7 and CNNM3 showed similar results (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), compatible with a TRPM7 Mg2+ permeability unaltered by co-expression of CNNM3, regardless of the heterologous expression system.
evidence: This is a finding from patch-clamp experiments in HEK293 cells shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: TRPM7 Mg2+ permeability is unaltered by co-expression of CNNM3.
source: Corresponding experiments with cells co-expressing TRPM7 and CNNM3 showed similar results (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), compatible with a TRPM7 Mg2+ permeability unaltered by co-expression of CNNM3, regardless of the heterologous expression system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from patch-clamp experiments.

claim: Transient expression of TRPM7 increased the cellular Mg content.
source: Next, we normalised the levels of magnesium to cellular sulphur (a biomarker for the total protein content) and observed that transient expression of TRPM7 increased the cellular Mg content, whereas expression of CNNM3 did not change this parameter (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from ICP-MS analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Expression of CNNM3 did not change cellular Mg content.
source: Next, we normalised the levels of magnesium to cellular sulphur (a biomarker for the total protein content) and observed that transient expression of TRPM7 increased the cellular Mg content, whereas expression of CNNM3 did not change this parameter (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from ICP-MS analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Co-expression of TRPM7 with CNNM3 did not impact the ability of TRPM7 to regulate the cellular content of Mg2+.
source: Importantly, we found that co-expression of TRPM7 with CNNM3 did not impact the ability of TRPM7 to regulate the cellular content of Mg2+ (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from ICP-MS analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: CNNM3 acts as a negative regulator of the TRPM7 kinase activity.
source: Co-expression of CNNM3 however caused a significant reduction of the (p)Ser1511 TRPM7 signal (Figure 5), suggesting that CNNM3 functions as a negative regulator of the TRPM7 kinase.
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Exposure of living cells to TG100-115 led to suppression of (p)Ser1511 TRPM7 immunoreactivity in a dose-dependent fashion.
source: We observed that the exposure of living cells to TG100-115 led to suppression of (p)Ser1511 TRPM7 immunoreactivity in a dose-dependent fashion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The inhibitory effect of TG100-115 on TRPM7 kinase was time-dependent and could be detected 10 min after application.
source: Moreover, the inhibitory effect of TG100-115 was time-dependent and could be detected 10 min after application of TG100-115 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Wash-out of TG100-115 by fresh cell culture medium caused a fast recovery of the (p)Ser1511 TRPM7 signal.
source: Furthermore, we found that wash-out of TG100-115 by fresh cell culture medium caused a fast recovery of the (p)Ser1511 TRPM7 signal (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Co-expression of ARL15 did not modulate TRPM7 kinase activity.
source: Accordingly, we investigated whether co-expression of ARL15 could modulate TRPM7 kinase activity and found no changes in (p)Ser1511 TRPM7 immunoreactivity (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: TRPM7 purified from rodent brain and transfected HEK293 cells showed very similar patterns of serine and threonine phosphorylation.
source: Thus, TRPM7 purified either from rodent brain or from transfected HEK293 cells showed very similar patterns of serine and threonine phosphorylation, reflected by matching MS/MS spectra of peptides harbouring phosphorylation sites (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 2 to Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from MS/MS analysis shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Four phosphorylation sites (S1300, S1360, T1466, and S1567) have not been reported for TRPM7 in native tissue before.
source: Out of the nine shared phospho-sites, four have not been reported for TRPM7 in native tissue before (S1300, S1360, T1466, and S1567; Supplementary file 2 to Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from MS/MS analysis.

claim: An additional 26 phosphorylated serine and threonine residues could be assigned to TRPM7 isolated from HEK 293 cells.
source: An additional 26 phosphorylated serine and threonine residues could be assigned to TRPM7 isolated from HEK 293 cells, presumably based on the higher amounts of TRPM7 available for analysis from heterologous (over)-expression material; 22 of these 26 sites match sites previously reported for TRPM7 endogenously or heterologously expressed in cell lines, and four sites were newly detected (S1208, S1480, S1496, S1853; Supplementary file 2 to Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from MS/MS analysis.

claim: Four newly detected phosphorylation sites in HEK293 cells are S1208, S1480, S1496, and S1853.
source: An additional 26 phosphorylated serine and threonine residues could be assigned to TRPM7 isolated from HEK 293 cells, presumably based on the higher amounts of TRPM7 available for analysis from heterologous (over)-expression material; 22 of these 26 sites match sites previously reported for TRPM7 endogenously or heterologously expressed in cell lines, and four sites were newly detected (S1208, S1480, S1496, S1853; Supplementary file 2 to Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from MS/MS analysis.

claim: Most of the identified phosphorylation sites were found to cluster within the C-terminal cytoplasmic domain of TRPM7.
source: Most of the identified phosphorylation sites were found to cluster within the C-terminal cytoplasmic domain of TRPM7.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from MS/MS analysis.

claim: Three TRPM7 mutants (S1208D, S1496D, and S1567D) displayed enhanced current amplitudes.
source: We introduced phosphomimetic mutations in a subset of identified phospho-sites (S1208D, S1360D, S1480D, S1496D, and S1567D) and found that three TRPM7 mutants (S1208D, S1496D, and S1567D) displayed enhanced current amplitudes (Figure 6B and C), whereas their expression levels were similar to WT TRPM7 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a finding from TEVC measurements shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: The expression levels of S1208D, S1496D, and S1567D mutants were similar to WT TRPM7.
source: We introduced phosphomimetic mutations in a subset of identified phospho-sites (S1208D, S1360D, S1480D, S1496D, and S1567D) and found that three TRPM7 mutants (S1208D, S1496D, and S1567D) displayed enhanced current amplitudes (Figure 6B and C), whereas their expression levels were similar to WT TRPM7 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Phosphorylation of TRPM7 may represent a new regulatory mechanism.
source: These findings suggest that phosphorylation of TRPM7 may represent a new regulatory mechanism reminiscent of the situation with TRPM8 (Rivera et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phosphomimetic mutant experiments with a citation to similar findings in TRPM8.

claim: The C-terminal α-kinase domain of TRPM7 autophosphorylates cytoplasmic residues of TRPM7.
source: The C-terminal α-kinase domain of TRPM7 acts in two ways: First, it autophosphorylates cytoplasmic residues of TRPM7, and second, it may target a variety of proteins with diverse cellular functions such as annexin A1, myosin II, eEF2-k, PLCγ2, STIM2, SMAD2, and RhoA (Runnels et al., 2001; Dorovkov and Ryazanov, 2004; Perraud et al., 2011; Clark et al., 2008; Romagnani et al., 2017; Voringer et al., 2020; Faouzi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: The TRPM7 kinase domain may target a variety of proteins with diverse cellular functions such as annexin A1, myosin II, eEF2-k, PLCγ2, STIM2, SMAD2, and RhoA.
source: The C-terminal α-kinase domain of TRPM7 acts in two ways: First, it autophosphorylates cytoplasmic residues of TRPM7, and second, it may target a variety of proteins with diverse cellular functions such as annexin A1, myosin II, eEF2-k, PLCγ2, STIM2, SMAD2, and RhoA (Runnels et al., 2001; Dorovkov and Ryazanov, 2004; Perraud et al., 2011; Clark et al., 2008; Romagnani et al., 2017; Voringer et al., 2020; Faouzi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: In immune cells, the TRPM7 kinase domain has been reported to be clipped from the channel domain by caspases in response to Fas-receptor stimulation.
source: In immune cells, the TRPM7 kinase domain has been reported to be clipped from the channel domain by caspases in response to Fas-receptor stimulation (Desai et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.

claim: Cleaved TRPM7 kinase was detected in several cell lines and shown to translocate to the nucleus, where it promotes histone phosphorylation.
source: In line with this observation, cleaved TRPM7 kinase was detected in several cell lines and shown to translocate to the nucleus, where it promotes histone phosphorylation (Krapivinsky et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.

claim: There are four members of the CNNM gene family in mammals: CNNM1-4.
source: There are four family members in mammals, CNNM1-4, widely expressed in the body and abundantly present in the brain (Funato and Miki, 2019; Giménez-Mascarell et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: CNNM1-4 are widely expressed in the body and abundantly present in the brain.
source: There are four family members in mammals, CNNM1-4, widely expressed in the body and abundantly present in the brain (Funato and Miki, 2019; Giménez-Mascarell et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: Genetic inactivation of Cnnm4 in mice leads to systemic Mg2+ deficiency.
source: The genetic inactivation of Cnnm4 in mice leads to systemic Mg2+ deficiency (Yamazaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.

claim: In humans, point mutations in CNNM2 cause hypomagnesemia.
source: In humans, point mutations in CNNM2 cause hypomagnesemia (Stuiver et al., 2011), while mutations in CNNM4 are associated with Jalili syndrome (Parry et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.

claim: Mutations in CNNM4 are associated with Jalili syndrome.
source: In humans, point mutations in CNNM2 cause hypomagnesemia (Stuiver et al., 2011), while mutations in CNNM4 are associated with Jalili syndrome (Parry et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.

claim: Functional expression studies proposed that CNNMs operate as Na+/Mg2+ exchangers responsible for the efflux of cytosolic Mg2+ from the cell.
source: Functional expression studies proposed that CNNMs operate as Na+/Mg2+ exchangers responsible for the efflux of cytosolic Mg2+ from the cell (Funato and Miki, 2019; Giménez-Mascarell et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: Other investigators proposed that CNNM proteins indirectly regulate the influx of Mg2+ into the cell.
source: In contrast to this view, other investigators proposed that CNNM proteins indirectly regulate the influx of Mg2+ into the cell (Arjona and de Baaij, 2018).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.

claim: Recently resolved crystal structures of two prokaryotic CNNM-like proteins revealed that CNNMs form dimers.
source: Recently resolved crystal structures of two prokaryotic CNNM-like proteins revealed that CNNMs form dimers and that each monomer contains three transmembrane helices harbouring Mg2+ and Na+ binding sites consistent with the suggested Na+-coupled Mg2+ transport function of CNNMs (Huang et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: Each CNNM monomer contains three transmembrane helices harbouring Mg2+ and Na+ binding sites.
source: Recently resolved crystal structures of two prokaryotic CNNM-like proteins revealed that CNNMs form dimers and that each monomer contains three transmembrane helices harbouring Mg2+ and Na+ binding sites consistent with the suggested Na+-coupled Mg2+ transport function of CNNMs (Huang et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: The direct association of TRPM7 with CNNMs suggests that TRPM7-mediated influx of divalent cations and CNNM-dependent Na+/Mg2+ exchange can be physically coupled under native conditions.
source: While the majority of CNNM proteins in a cell is not bound to TRPM7, the direct association identified in this study suggests a new concept implying that two transporting mechanisms, TRPM7-mediated influx of divalent cations (Zn2+, Mg2+, and Ca2+) and CNNM-dependent Na+/Mg2+ exchange, can be physically coupled under native conditions, thus, warranting future studies to examine the exact functional interplay between the channel-kinase TRPM7 and CNNMs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings of the study.

claim: ARL15 is a member of the ARF gene family of small G-proteins.
source: ARL15 is a member of the ARF gene family of small G-proteins (Gillingham and Munro, 2007).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.

claim: A common feature of ARFs is their ability to bind and regulate effector proteins in a GTP-dependent manner.
source: A common feature of ARFs is their ability to bind and regulate effector proteins in a GTP-dependent manner (Gillingham and Munro, 2007).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.

claim: GDP- and GTP-bound states of ARFs are controlled by GTPase-activating proteins (GAP) in conjunction with GTP exchange factors (GEF).
source: GDP- and GTP-bound states of ARFs are controlled by GTPase-activating proteins (GAP) in conjunction with GTP exchange factors (GEF) (Gillingham and Munro, 2007).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.

claim: The best-characterised ARFs are involved in membrane trafficking, phospholipid metabolism and remodelling of the cytoskeleton.
source: The best-characterised ARFs are involved in membrane trafficking, phospholipid metabolism and remodelling of the cytoskeleton (Gillingham and Munro, 2007).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to previous literature.
